text: Long ago. <break time="0.8s" /> Under a different name, Adolph Myers. <break time="0.8s" /> Wing Biddlebaum had been a teacher. <break time="0.8s" /> In a small town in Pennsylvania. <break time="0.8s" /> Where the boys of his school loved him. <break time="0.8s" /> He was one of those rare men. <break time="0.8s" /> Who are meant by nature to teach the young. <break time="0.8s" /> And he ruled his pupils. <break time="0.8s" /> Not by force but by a gentle power. <break time="0.8s" /> In the evening. <break time="0.8s" /> He walked with the boys. <break time="0.8s" /> Or sat talking with them on the schoolhouse steps. <break time="0.8s" /> And his voice became soft and musical. <break time="0.8s" /> As he spoke. <break time="0.8s" /> His hands moved as he talked. <break time="0.8s" /> Patting the boys shoulders now and then. <break time="0.8s" /> For through his hands. <break time="0.8s" /> He tried to put his dreams. <break time="0.8s" /> Into their young minds. <break time="0.8s" /> Under that gentle touch. <break time="0.8s" /> Doubt and disbelief went out of the boys. <break time="0.8s" /> And they too began to dream. <break time="0.8s" /> Which was exactly what their teacher had hoped for. <break time="0.8s" /> Then a confused boy of the school. <break time="0.8s" /> Misunderstood his teachers kindness. <break time="0.8s" /> And told a strange, untrue story about him. <break time="0.8s" /> As if it were a fact. <break time="0.8s" /> The parents believed the story. <break time="0.8s" /> And the gentle touch. <break time="0.8s" /> That had come from his care for the boys. <break time="0.8s" /> Was now seen as something to fear. <break time="0.8s" /> One dark, rainy night. <break time="0.8s" /> A crowd of angry men. <break time="0.8s" /> Came to his house with lanterns. <break time="0.8s" /> And they drove him out of town. <break time="0.8s" /> Into the darkness.
